item.title: Eisa Guide: Okinawa's Drum Dance, Festivals & Where to See It
item.description: Eisa is Okinawa’s electrifying traditional drum-and-dance — rows of performers in vivid costume pounding taiko drums and spinning to the call of the sanshin, all driven by a hypnotic chant and whistle. Rooted in Obon ceremonies to honour ancestral spirits, eisa has grown into a proud symbol of Okinawan identity performed at festivals, cultural parks and street events. The spectacular Okinawa Zento (“All-Island”) Eisa Festival in Okinawa City each autumn is the grandest gathering of all.

item.title: Ryukyu Mura Guide: Tickets, Eisa Shows & Access
item.description: Ryukyu Mura is an open-air theme park in Onna, central Okinawa, that recreates the look and life of an old Ryukyu Kingdom village. Relocated traditional houses with red-tiled roofs and guardian shisa, costumed staff, lively eisa drum-and-dance performances, sanshin music and hands-on craft workshops make it an easy, family-friendly introduction to Okinawan culture. It’s a popular stop on the way up the west coast toward the Churaumi Aquarium. This guide covers the village, performances, craft experiences, tickets and how to get there.

item.title: Okinawa Festivals Guide: Eisa, Dragon Boats, Lanterns & Ryukyuan Ceremonies
item.description: Okinawa’s festival calendar reflects its unique heritage — Ryukyuan religious ceremonies, Obon customs distinct from mainland Japan, and a performance tradition centred on the eisa drum dance and sanshin music that has no equivalent anywhere else. The events are not recreations for tourists; they are living community traditions. 旧盆エイサー — Okinawan Eisa (Obon Period) When: Three days of Obon by the lunar calendar — typically mid-to-late August Where: Every village and neighbourhood across Okinawa; biggest in Okinawa City (Koza)
